question.leadin: A certain city's boule oversaw the process for dealing this kind of punishment, which required 6000 votes to be carried out.
question.text: Name this kind of punishment,which was dealt to people who were ostracized in ancient Athens.

swap.leadin: After this battle, Pheidippides ran approximately 26 miles to Athens to announce a Greek victory.
swap.text: Name this 490 BCE battle that lends its name to a very long race.
swap.clue: Datis and Artaphernes were stopped from moving inland by the presence of troops positioned in a swamp, led by Miltiades.

question.leadin: Name these Wonders of the Ancient World.
question.text: This tall bronze statue on the island of Rhodes was not, in fact, tall enough to span the harbor, but few people could link their arms around one of its thumbs.
question.clue: An Egyptian offer to rebuild this structure was refused after a 226 BCE earthquake destroyed it.

swap.leadin: In 336 BCE, this man succeeded his father, Philip II; within two years, he had pacified Greece and started an invasion of Persia.
swap.text: Name this "Great" Macedonian leader, whose Hellenistic empire eventually stretched to India before he died at the age of 32.
swap.clue: Along with his father, this man's forces beat the Sacred Band of Thebes.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Panhellenic games.
question.text: The Pythian games occurred in this city, which the Greeks believed was the center of the world. This city was the site of a priestess of Apollo, sometimes called the Pythia.
question.clue: An outcrop known as Sibyl's Rock overlooks the Temple of Apollo in this city, where the ruins of the Tholos temple can be seen, and its sloped theatre provides a view of the valley of Phocis.

swap.leadin: The collapse of this civilization led to the "Greek Dark Ages."
swap.text: Name this Bronze Age civilization in modern day Greece, whose language was discovered on the Linear B tablet.
swap.clue: An artifact from this culture depicts a handlebar mustache and beard on a gold burial mask.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about war in Ancient Greece.
question.text: This nearly thirty-year-long war between Athens and Sparta was vividly recounted by Thucydides. The Athenian general Pericles died of plague early in this war.
question.clue: One side in this war laid siege to Melos, where a dialogue apocryphally occurred containing the aphorism "the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must."

swap.leadin: Name these things about the Persian Wars.
swap.text: Leonidas and three hundred Spartans died defending a narrow mountain path in this battle.
swap.clue: During this battle, a force including Demophilus' Thespians was attacked from behind after Ephialtes ("eh-fi-AL-tees") revealed a Phocian-guarded path to Xerxes.

question.leadin: According to Diodorus Siculus, this leader was assassinated by a member of his bodyguard who had been replaced as his lover by a youth with the same name.
question.text: Name this leader, who defeated an alliance of various Greek city-states at the 338 BCE Battle of Chaeronea ("CHAY-roe-NAY-uh").
question.answerHtml: Philip II [or Philippos II; accept, but DO NOT REVEAL, Philip II of Macedon; prompt on Philip]
question.clue: This man's half-brother John of Austria helped him crush the Morisco Revolt.

swap.text: The Spartans lost control of the Delian League following the abuses of the Spartan general Pausanias, a nephew of this king. This king died fighting the Persians at Thermopylae.
swap.clue: Simonides commemorated a group led by this man with an epitaph addressed to a "stranger passing by."

question.leadin: Legendarily during this battle, a female apparition chastised a navy for backing their ships away.
question.text: Name this September 480 B.C. naval battle fought near the namesake straits, which was won by Greek forces under Themistocles. It is considered one of the pivotal battles in the Greco-Persian War.
question.clue: The losing commander built a throne on Mount Aigaleo to observe this battle, which was fought after a stalemate at Artemisium.

swap.leadin: Name these figures from the Peloponnesian War.
swap.text: This Spartan admiral commanded the fleet which triumphed over Athens at the Battle of Aegospotami in 405 B.C.
swap.clue: This beneficiary of Cyrus the Younger's patronage resumed his most famous office after his replacement Callicratidas lost the battle of Arginusae.

question.text: This civilization who wrote in Linear A is said to possibly be part of the Sea Peoples. This Aegean culture built a palace at Knossos and is named after a mythical king who ordered a king of Athens to send 14 young people to his domain at tribute.
question.clue: A devastating blow this civilization occurred when the Thera volcano erupted in the 16th century BCE, which contributed to their eventual decline and the occupation by the Mycenaean Greeks.

swap.leadin: Answer questions about Sparta that have absolutely nothing to do with Thermopylae or Frank Miller graphic novels.
swap.text: The slave class of Sparta consisted of these people, who were mostly conquered. Pausanias lead them in revolt in the 5th century BC.
swap.clue: Epaminondas dissolved one group of these people after the Battle of Leuctra.

question.leadin: Emmett Bennett's standardization efforts helped the completion of this task, which was met with initial skepticism until scholars examined the tripod tablet uncovered by Carl Blegen.
question.text: Name this task completed by Michael Ventris, who published a monograph on its results with John Chadwick. Objects found at Tiryns and Pylos helped complete this task.

swap.leadin: Herodotus wrote that holders of this position had sole jurisdiction over who should marry unbetrothed heiresses and matters concerning public roads.
swap.text: Name this hereditary position held simultaneously by members of the Agiad and Eurypontid families, both of whom claimed descent from Heracles. This office's powers were kept in check by both the gerousia and the ephors.
swap.answerHtml: kings of Sparta [or archagetai; prompt on basileus or kings or monarchs by asking “of what state?”]
swap.clue: These rulers were descended in two lines from the twins Procles and Eurysthenes, and ruled in a diarchy.

question.leadin: Plutarch claims that the kings Polydorus and Theopompus inserted a clause into this document saying it shall be lawful for the leaders to dissolve if the people are crooked.
question.text: Name this questionably-historical document which laid down the laws of Sparta after Lycurgus obtained its instructions from an oracle.

swap.leadin: One ruler of this name was accused by Polybius of murdering his predecessor, Archidamus V, although Archidamus was probably murdered by the same people who did in his brother, Agis IV.
swap.text: Identify this name shared by two kings of Sparta, the third of which preceded Archidamus and the first of which invaded Athens in 510 B.C.E. to depose the tyrant Hippias.

question.leadin: The second ruler of this name commissioned the ship Syracusia.
question.text: Give this name of two rulers of Syracuse, the first of whom defeated the Etruscans at the Battle of Cumae, and the second of whom patronised Archimedes.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about wars from Archaic Greek history that we don't really know anything about, FTPE.
swap.text: A series of wars in the eighth and seventh centuries led to Sparta's conquest of this region of the Peloponnese, whose inhabitants were the original Helots.
swap.clue: This Peloponnesian region that fought three wars, including two in the Archaic Period, with a neighboring polis. Demand for this region's fertile land, or kleroi, likely helped cause the first of those conflicts.
